name: rsid
label: RSID (automatic digital-mode ID)
description: RSID (RSID / Reed-Solomon Identifier) is fldigi's automatic mode-detection beacon: a short, robust 16-tone burst many digital-mode operators transmit just before their traffic to announce which mode and centre frequency follow. This preset runs the fldigi RSID detector continuously and, the moment it recognises a burst, hot-swaps the decoder to the announced mode (RTTY, PSK31, MT63, Olivia, Contestia, DominoEX, Throb, …) — no manual mode picking. It starts in RTTY (rtty45) until the first RSID fires. Tune so the signal sits around the 1500 Hz audio sweet spot (dial ≈ signal − 1.5 kHz); AFC tracks. Park it on a busy 20 m digimode watering hole (14.070–14.100 MHz USB; also 7.040–7.100, 3.580–3.600, 10.130–10.150, 21.070–21.100, 28.070–28.120) and it will follow whatever mode shows up. Decoded text streams under the decoder::fldigi log target; mode switches under decoder::rsid. Audio is teed alongside so you can listen.
ai_notes: RSID auto digital-mode detect (vendored fldigi, FldigiAuto block). Starts in rtty45; on an RSID burst it rebuilds the inner modem to the detected mode in place (same block id/wiring) and logs the switch to `decoder::rsid`. Decoded text: `tail decoder --category fldigi`; detections: `tail decoder --category rsid`. Best on busy digimode watering holes (USB): 14.070–14.100 / 7.040–7.100 / 3.580–3.600 / 10.130–10.150 / 21.070–21.100 / 28.070–28.120 MHz. Output is continuous (no slots); many ops send RSID before each over, so detections are bursty — wait for activity. Weak copy is usually antenna/AGC, not the detector — fixed gain + AGC off helps on quiet bands. Not every mode RSIDs; silent operators won't auto-switch.
